headline: Your voice shapes our curriculum—every learner can contribute to making lessons better
universal_truth: The best curricula are living documents, improved by the community that uses them
fun_facts: You can leave feedback on any phase of any lesson—not just the whole lesson
Accepted suggestions get credited to the contributor
Our curriculum has been improved hundreds of times by learner input
discussion_questions: What would make this lesson better?
Have you noticed something that could be clearer or more accurate?
What topics are missing that you wish we covered?

hook.script: Every lesson you take has a feedback button. Not for the whole lesson—for each phase. See something wrong? Have a better example? Want to share an insight? Your voice matters, and we're listening.

cliff.script: Why would a curriculum invite criticism? Isn't that risky?

options.text: Learners see what creators miss—you experience the lesson fresh, notice confusions, have real-world examples; crowdsourced improvement makes better education for everyone
options.response: Exactly. We can't see our own blind spots. Learners bring fresh perspectives, diverse experiences, and real-world testing. Your feedback makes everyone's learning better.
That's why we review every suggestion before implementation. Quality control plus community input equals the best of both worlds...

fact1.title: Per-Phase Feedback
fact1.script: Notice the comment icon on each phase? That's where you share insights, questions, or suggestions specific to that moment in the lesson. Precise feedback helps us make precise improvements.

fact2.title: The Commons
fact2.script: The Commons is our community space where all feedback lives. Browse what others have shared, vote on suggestions you agree with, and see which improvements have been implemented. It's curriculum democracy.

fact3.title: Types of Contributions
fact3.script: You can share insights from your experience, ask questions that others might share, suggest corrections or improvements, or offer alternative examples. Every type of contribution helps.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Education improves when learners have voice. You're not just consuming—you're contributing. That makes you part of something bigger.

outro.script: That's how to improve the curriculum. Start noticing what could be better, and share it. Your insights might help thousands of future learners.

growTrack.title: First Contribution - Share One Insight
growTrack.activity: Go to any lesson you've completed. Find one phase that sparked a thought—an insight, question, or suggestion. Use the comment button to share it. You've just contributed to the curriculum.
